extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency staff and attorneys responsible for drafting and submitting Federal Register notices, proposed rules, codifications, and Privacy Act records requests procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for drafting part headings, tables of contents, citations, incorporations by reference, placement of authority citations, preparation of notices and proposed rules, and agency Privacy Act procedures for records access, correction, and disclosure. Targeted at agencies preparing documents for the Federal Register and CFR codification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part heading descriptive requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: a brief descriptive heading, preceding the text, on a separate line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each part heading shall indicate briefly the general subject matter of the part; avoid nondiscriptive phrases such as 'Regulations under the Act of July 28, 1955' or introductory expressions like 'Regulations governing' and 'Rules applicable to' (§§21.18, 21.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and content of table of contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of contents shall be used at the beginning of the part whenever a new part is introduced, an existing part is completely revised, or a group of sections is revised or added and set forth as a subpart or otherwise separately grouped under a center head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table shall follow the part heading and precede the text of the regulations in that part; it shall list headings for subparts, undesignated center headings, sections in the part, and appendix headings to the part or subpart (§21.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of part headings (prohibitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part headings must indicate general subject matter and must not use expressions that are not descriptive of the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases such as 'Regulations under the Act of July 28, 1955' and introductory expressions like 'Regulations governing' and 'Rules applicable to' may not be used (§21.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendatory document identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendatory document shall identify in specific terms the unit amended, and the extent of the changes made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number and heading of each section amended shall be set forth in full on a separate line (§21.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision in references to the Code of Federal Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reference to the Code of Federal Regulations shall be in terms of the specific titles, chapters, parts, sections, and paragraphs involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambiguous references such as 'herein', 'above', 'below', and similar expressions may not be used. Each document that contains a reference to material published in the Code shall include the Code citation as part of the reference (§21.21(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of agency regulations in full text (cross-reference exception rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall publish its own regulations in full text; cross-references to the regulations of another agency may not be used as a substitute for publication in full text except in listed exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where cross-references may be used include: (1) reference required by court order/statute/Executive order/reorganization plan; (2) reference to regulations promulgated by an agency with exclusive legal authority that must be applied by the referencing agency; (3) reference is informational or improves clarity rather than regulatory; (4) reference to Federal agency test methods/consensus standards that have replaced or preempted private/voluntary standards; (5) reference to Department-level from a subagency (§21.21(c)(1)–(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel citation formats for CFR and Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: For parallel reference, the Code of Federal Regulations and the FEDERAL REGISTER may be cited in specified forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable forms include 'lll CFR lll (lll FR lll). § lll' and 'of this chapter (lll FR lll)' (§21.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: References to historical Code editions
rubrics_metrics.description: When referencing material codified in the 1938 edition of the CFR or supplements, specific historical citation forms may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'lll CFR, 1938 Ed., lll.'; 'lll CFR, 1943, Cum. Supp., lll.'; 'lll CFR, 1946 Supp., lll.' (§21.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document subject to codification shall include a clear statement as to the date or dates upon which its contents become effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear effective date or dates must be included in codified documents (§21.30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of OMB control numbers in regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: To display OMB control numbers in agency regulations, those numbers shall be placed parenthetically at the end of the section or displayed in a table or codified section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB control numbers may be parenthetical at the section end, or shown in a table or a codified section (§21.35).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section in a document subject to codification must include, or be covered by, a complete citation of the authority under which the section is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations must include general or specific statutory authority delegated by statute and executive delegations, if any, necessary to link the statutory authority to the issuing agency (§21.40).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility for authority citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each issuing agency is responsible for the accuracy and integrity of the citations of authority in the documents it issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each issuing agency shall formally amend the citations of authority in its codified material to reflect any changes therein (§21.41).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director exception to citation placement/form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register may make exceptions to placement and form requirements relating to citations of authority when strict application would impair practical use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director discretion available when strict application would impair practical use of citations (§21.42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement rules for authority citations when setting out entire CFR part
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document sets out an entire CFR part, the agency shall place the complete authority citation directly after the table of contents and before the regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency shall set out the full text of the authority citation for each part affected by the document (§21.43(a)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement rules for authority citations when amending certain sections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document amends only certain sections within a CFR part, the agency shall present the complete authority citation to this part as the first item in the list of amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the authority for issuing an amendment is the same as that listed for the whole CFR part, restate the authority; if the authority changes, revise the authority citation in its entirety and may specify particular authority under which certain sections are amended (§21.43(a)(2),(i),(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized authority citation presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall present a centralized authority citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authority citation shall appear at the end of the table of contents for a part or after each subpart heading within the text of a part. Citations for particular sections may be specified within the centralized authority citation (§21.43(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory authority citation ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation to a nonstatutory document as authority shall be placed after the statutory citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format provided: list statutory citations first then nonstatutory ones such as Executive Orders and FR citations (§21.45).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of formal authority citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal citations of authority shall be in the shortest form compatible with positive identification and ready reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of the Federal Register shall assist agencies in developing model citations (§21.51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory material citation specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: All citations to statutory authority shall include a United States Code citation, where available; citations to Public Laws and U.S. Statutes at Large are optional when the USC is cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations to current public laws and Statutes at Large shall refer to the section and volume/page assigned; examples provided (§21.52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of nonstatutory materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstatutory documents shall be cited by document designation and by FEDERAL REGISTER volume and page, followed, if possible, by the parallel citation to the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: list special civil air reg., FR citation, CFR part, and Executive Order citations as applicable (§21.53).

rubrics_metrics.name: Name and caption requirements for Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the agency issuing a notice shall be placed at the beginning of the document; when a specific bureau or unit issues a notice its name shall be on a separate line under the agency name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File numbers, docket numbers, or similar identifying symbols shall be placed in brackets immediately below headings; provide a suitable short title on a separate line immediately after other captions; where appropriate include an additional brief caption indicating the nature of the document (§22.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation form for Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority under which an agency issues a notice shall be cited in narrative form within text or in parentheses on a separate line following text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency notices must include an authority citation either in narrative form or parenthetical on its own line (§22.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of proposed rule documents (statement of proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed rule required by section 553 of title 5 or any similar document shall include a statement of the time, place, and nature of public rulemaking proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also must include reference to the authority under which the regulatory action is proposed (§22.5(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Code designation placement for proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The area of the Code of Federal Regulations directly affected by a proposed regulatory action shall be identified by placing the appropriate CFR citation immediately below the name of the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: '1 CFR part 22' directly under agency name (§22.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification of proposed full-text regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any part of a proposed rule document that contains the full text of a proposed regulation shall also conform to the pertinent provisions of part 21 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-text provisions in proposals must follow part 21 formatting and related requirements (§22.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on incorporation by reference and legal limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation by reference is intended to benefit the Federal Government and affected classes and is not intended to detract from legal or practical attributes of publication; incorporation is limited to the edition approved and future amendments or revisions are not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will interpret 5 U.S.C. 552(a) together with other publication requirements and will apply part 51 standards fairly and uniformly; publication in the Federal Register of a document containing an incorporation does not itself constitute Director approval (§51.1(a)–(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for Director approval of incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will approve incorporation by reference when: (1) publication is eligible (§51.7); (2) language of incorporation meets requirements (§51.9); (3) publication is on file with the Office of the Federal Register; and (4) Director has received a written request from the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director will notify agency of approval or disapproval within 20 working days after agency has met all requirements (§51.3(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency timeline and materials for requesting approval
rubrics_metrics.description: For timely approval an agency must make a written request at least 20 working days before submitting the final rule, send a copy of the final rule using the proper language of incorporation, and ensure a copy of the publication is on file at the Office of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal approval applies to a final rule document; agencies may consult with the Office at any time (§51.5(a)(1)–(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for publications to be incorporated by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication is eligible if it conforms to policy in §51.1; is published data/criteria/standards/specifications/techniques/illustrations or similar material; substantially reduces the volume published in the Federal Register; and is reasonably available to and usable by the class of persons affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In assessing usability the Director will consider completeness and ease of handling and whether the publication is bound, numbered, and organized. The Director will assume agency-produced publications are inappropriate unless unique; publications previously published in the Federal Register or in the United States Code are not appropriate (§51.7(a)–(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements of proper incorporation language
rubrics_metrics.description: The language incorporating a publication by reference shall be as precise and complete as possible and shall make it clear that incorporation is intended and completed by the final rule document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper incorporation language should (1) use the words 'incorporated by reference'; (2) state title, date, edition, author, publisher, and number of the publication; (3) inform the user the incorporated publication is a requirement; (4) make official showing where/how copies may be examined and readily obtained with maximum convenience to the user; and (5) refer to 5 U.S.C. 552(a). If Director approves, agency must include under DATES caption the approval statement and include 'incorporation by reference' in index terms (§51.9(b),(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to change or remove an approved incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency seeking approval for a change to an approved incorporation must publish notice of the change in the Federal Register and amend the Code of Federal Regulations, ensure a copy of the amendment or revision is on file at the Office of the Federal Register, and notify the Director in writing that the change is being made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a regulation containing an incorporation fails to become effective or is removed from the CFR, the agency must notify the Director in writing within 5 working days of the occurrence (§51.11(a),(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of existence of records (Privacy Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person wishing to know whether a system of records contains a record pertaining to him or her may appear in person at specified office hours or may write to the agency; requests are recommended to be in writing and, if by persons other than the individual, should state relationship to that individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests will not be honored unless made by the individual to whom the record pertains or by the individual's legal guardian if declared incompetent; Commission will acknowledge requests within 10 working days and normally notify existence/non-existence within 30 working days; no special identity verification required for individuals seeking to know existence (§425.2(a)–(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and timing for access to Privacy Act records
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may request review of records pertaining to him by appearing in person or writing; the Commission will strive to make the record available within 15 working days or to inform requester of need for additional identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable identification such as employment ID cards, driver’s licenses, or credit cards will normally be accepted for in-person requests; charges for copies are $0.10 per photocopy with thresholds: no charge unless computed charge would exceed $3; if fee > $25 requester is notified and must tender fee before copying; remittances by personal check, bank draft drawn on U.S. bank, or money order payable to the Treasury and sent to Administrative Officer; individuals will not be denied access (§425.3(a)–(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and amendment of Privacy Act records (request content and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may request that records be amended or corrected by written request to the Administrative Officer; the signature is sufficient identification and the request must contain exact description of items to be amended, reasons, and birthdate for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 10 working days the Administrative Officer shall acknowledge receipt (unless processed within ten days); requester will be notified within 30 days whether request granted. If amendment appropriate to make record relevant/necessary and accurate, Officer shall change the record, advise requester within 30 days, and advise prior recipients after accounting; if denied, explain reasons within 30 days and inform requester of right to Director review within 30 days; Director to review within 30 working days and follow-up actions listed (§425.4(a)–(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights after denial of Privacy Act amendment request
rubrics_metrics.description: If agency denies amendment, requester may file a concise statement of disagreement; the record will be annotated to indicate the statement and it will be made available to anyone to whom the record is disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must notify prior recipients who still retain copies after accounting; agency officials may include a brief summary of reasons for refusal in future disclosures; advise requester of right to judicial review under 5 U.S.C. 552a(g)(1)(A) (§425.4(f),(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Privacy Act records to third parties (conditions and accounting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records subject to the Privacy Act requested by any person other than the individual will not be made available except under specified circumstances and an accounting of each disclosure will be indicated on the record and is available to the individual on written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example permitted disclosure: circulating records to appropriate officials incident to placing Fellows in work assignments; accounting includes date, nature, purpose of disclosure and name/address of recipient (§425.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for Privacy Act procedures (record/system/routine use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'individual', 'maintain', 'record', 'system of records', and 'routine use' are defined for purposes of the Commission's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'record' includes any information about an individual maintained by the Commission that contains name or identifying number; 'system of records' means records retrievable by name or identifying number; 'routine use' means disclosure compatible with the purpose for which info was collected (§455.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting existence and access of records (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who wishes to know whether a system of records contains a record shall submit a written request to the System Manager, who shall within 10 days inform the individual whether such a record exists; requests for access shall indicate whether the individual intends to appear or receive copies by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors §455.3(a)–(b) requirements for National Capital Planning Commission system managers (§455.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements and hours for in-person Privacy Act requests (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals appearing in person must do so at the Commission’s offices between specified hours and present identification (driver’s license, employee ID) to permit verification; mail requests must include date and location of birth as proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If those forms of identification are not feasible, Commission may request a signed statement asserting identity and warning that knowingly seeking access to another's records under false pretenses is punishable by fine up to $5,000 (§455.4(a)–(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure upon verification and accounting (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon verification of identity the System Manager shall disclose to the individual the information contained in the record which pertains to that individual and the accounting of disclosures required by 5 U.S.C. 552a(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct disclosure to verified individual and provision of disclosure accounting as mandated (§455.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for correction or amendment (NCPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may request that a record be amended or corrected by submitting a request in accordance with §455.3 and stating the item sought to be amended and specific reasons therefor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency review procedures for correction/amendment follow in §455.7 (not fully shown in chunk) but initial request content and routing required (§455.6).
